verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {applicant_name}, the Applicant herein, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above application are true and correct to my personal knowledge. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Applicant

promptInstructions: Draft an application for appointment of receiver under Order 40 Rule 1 read with Section 151 CPC.

Standard: 'just and convenient' — court has wide discretion but exercises sparingly. Cite T. Krishnaswamy Chetty v. C. Thangavelu Chetty AIR 1955 Mad 430 — five principles for appointment of receiver: (i) just and convenient; (ii) plaintiff must show prima facie strong case; (iii) emergency / danger of waste; (iv) not interference unless necessary; (v) court must consider equity of conduct of applicant.
Most common in: partition suits, partnership dissolution, company oppression / mismanagement (Section 241 Companies Act), mortgage foreclosure, executions, trust administration.
Para 1: Reference to main suit, parties, relief sought.
Para 2: Description of subject property / business / undertaking (schedule, boundaries, account particulars).
Para 3: Current possession / management status.
Para 4: Specific acts / conduct of non-applicant showing waste, mismanagement, fraudulent dealing, dissipation, or deadlock.
Para 5: Why appointment is 'just and convenient' — emergency, irreparable risk, no alternative remedy adequate.
Para 6: Powers sought for receiver — manage, collect rents, maintain status quo, render accounts, sell with leave of court (sale always with leave).
Para 7: Proposed receiver (often a senior advocate, CA, or retired judicial officer) with consent letter; if not, leave it to court.
Para 8: Receiver's security under Order 40 R.3 — must give security as ordered.
Para 9: Remuneration under Order 40 R.2 — fixed by court (usually as % of receipts).
Para 10: Applicant's undertaking to indemnify in case appointment subsequently found improper.
Receiver is an officer of the court, not the party's agent. Acts of receiver bind the property, not the parties personally.
Receiver must render accounts at intervals fixed by court (Order 40 R.4).
Where partnership suit: receiver appointed at dissolution stage to wind up.
Where mortgage suit: receiver of mortgaged property pending sale.
Where matrimonial property / family business in dispute: receiver to preserve assets.
Caution: appointment of receiver dispossesses parties from their property — therefore extreme circumspection required. Cite Mannalal Khetan v. Kedar Nath Khetan (1977) 2 SCC 424.
Cite Maharwal Khewaji Trust v. Baldev Dass (2004) 8 SCC 488 — receiver should be appointed only as last resort.
Affidavit in support mandatory.
Append Lawie disclaimer.
